Authority input P0: Add a local batch importer for named records. One invalid item rejects the entire batch before persistence. Existing unrelated records remain byte-identical. This direction authorizes Design and delivery allocation, not implementation approval, publication, or retirement of existing regressions.

Model inputs: Child Input owns per-record validation; child Store owns record persistence. Parent Import owns validate-all-before-first-write and their combined atomic outcome. Supported batch is a nonempty list with distinct record names. Retry, concurrent-writer behavior and a network provider are outside this bounded example, not dispositions for the repository's actual models.

Candidate D0, compliant Markdown Design: IMP-SR-01 requires all records valid before any mutation, with all-or-none publication. IMP-SR-02 preserves unrelated record bytes. Parent coverage group Import atomicity cites both requirements and child guarantees. Violation: validating and writing in one loop can publish the first valid record before rejecting the second, losing atomicity. Consequence: partial user state that looks rejected. Private fixture: empty candidate names A/B plus unrelated sentinel Z with literal bytes 'keep\n'; A and B have independent literal expected contents. Valid partition: import valid A/B through the public import command, observe both exact contents, sentinel unchanged, exit0. Invalid partition: valid A then invalid B through the same command, observe named validation diagnostic, no A/B files, exact original sentinel, nonzero exit. Establish the valid fixture first; each run uses a fresh tree. Real filesystem/persistence stays inside the observation boundary. No mocks of the write path. Realization is proposed public integration proof, not claimed passing. Child parser tests alone do not establish this parent interaction. JSON is not required.

Candidate D1, one defining fault: Same P0, child contracts, requirements, fixture, group and interface as D0, but technical behavior writes each record immediately after validating it and keeps successful earlier writes when a later item fails. Its test expects A to exist after invalid B. Its prose still calls the operation atomic and includes the same requirement IDs.

Candidate L0, compliant delivery allocation: Require current independent approval of D0 before implementing. First establish a failing real public-command proof for invalid second record, with original tree snapshot and independent expected bytes. Then implement validate-all-before-write in one reviewable milestone, run valid and invalid partitions plus sentinel preservation, and hand exact diff/results to independent review. Preserve an existing regression R-old proving an unusual but supported character in a name; its absence from the group table does not authorize deletion. Cost measurement may prioritize fixture inspection, never waive IMP-SR-01/02. Missing observations block completeness. Results belong in evidence, not the living Design.

Candidate L1, one defining fault: Same D0 and delivery sequence as L0 but verification consists only of per-record parser return values; it claims this completes IMP-SR-01/02. It contains no public import or filesystem observation.

Candidate L2, one defining fault: Same D0 and complete public proof as L0, but remove R-old solely because it has no scenario catalog row and is slow. The protected name remains supported and no equivalent observation is identified.

Authority input P0: Add a local batch importer for named records. One invalid item rejects the entire batch before persistence. A persistence failure after writes are attempted must restore the original record set and report failure, never complete success. Existing unrelated records remain byte-identical. This direction authorizes Design and delivery allocation, not implementation approval, publication, or retirement of existing regressions.

Model inputs: Child Input owns per-record validation; child Store owns transaction-backed record persistence. Its declared transaction boundary can stage changes and abort them on a failed write; Import must use one transaction for the whole batch. Parent Import owns validate-all-before-first-write and their combined atomic outcome. Supported batch is a nonempty list with distinct record names. Retry, concurrent-writer behavior and a network provider are outside this bounded example, not dispositions for the repository's actual models.

Candidate D0, compliant Markdown Design: IMP-SR-01 requires all records valid before any mutation, with all-or-none publication on success and the original record set restored on persistence failure. The parent validates all items, then stages both writes in one Store transaction and commits only after both succeed; any failed write aborts that transaction and reports failure. IMP-SR-02 preserves unrelated record bytes. Parent coverage group Import atomicity cites both requirements and child guarantees. Violation: validating and writing in one loop can publish the first valid record before rejecting the second, losing atomicity. Consequence: partial user state that looks rejected. Private fixture: empty candidate names A/B plus unrelated sentinel Z with literal bytes 'keep\n'; A and B have independent literal expected contents. Valid partition: import valid A/B through the public import command, observe both exact contents, sentinel unchanged, exit0. Invalid partition: valid A then invalid B through the same command, observe named validation diagnostic, no A/B files, exact original sentinel, nonzero exit. Persistence-failure partition: establish the successful A/B control, then in a fresh copy invoke the real public import with a controlled storage fault on the second write, after observing the first A write attempt inside the same real transaction. Inspect the original record set independently: neither A nor B is committed, Z has exact original bytes, the named storage failure is reported with nonzero status and no complete-success result. Capture the attempted-write sequence to prove the defining fault was reached; no mocked store may supply the rollback result. Establish the valid fixture first; each run uses a fresh tree. Real filesystem/persistence stays inside the observation boundary. No mocks of the write path. Realization is proposed public integration proof, not claimed passing. Child parser tests alone do not establish this parent interaction. JSON is not required.

Candidate D1, one defining fault: Same P0, child contracts, requirements, fixture, group and interface as D0, but technical behavior writes each record immediately after validating it and keeps successful earlier writes when a later item fails. Its test expects A to exist after invalid B. Its prose still calls the operation atomic and includes the same requirement IDs.

Candidate L0, compliant delivery allocation: Require current independent approval of D0 before implementing. First establish failing real public-command proof for invalid second record and for the controlled second persistence-write failure after the first write attempt, with original tree snapshots, independent expected bytes and exact failure diagnostics. Keep real transaction/write/abort behavior inside those observations and establish a valid control before each defining fault. Then implement validate-all-before-write plus a single batch transaction in one reviewable milestone, run valid, invalid and persistence-failure partitions plus sentinel preservation, and hand exact diff/results to independent review. Preserve an existing regression R-old proving an unusual but supported character in a name; its absence from the group table does not authorize deletion. Cost measurement may prioritize fixture inspection, never waive IMP-SR-01/02. Missing observations block completeness. Results belong in evidence, not the living Design.
